role: For any real increments x1,...,xn of total zero whose partial sums s0,...,s_(n-1) are all distinct, prove the exact distribution over n cyclic rotations of N=#{1<=j<=n: rotated partial sum >=0}. Then derive the rotation-average exp(-lambda N). Explain ties and why grouping an exchangeable composition bridge into equal coarse blocks could create a log(R)/R scale. Do not assert an actual-array refutation.
public_findings: [{'type': 'surrogate_theorem', 'statement': 'Let s_0=0 and s_j=x_1+...+x_j, with s_n=0. For the rotation beginning after index k, 0<=k<n, its j-step partial sum equals s_{(k+j) mod n}-s_k, using periodicity s_{m+n}=s_m. As j ranges from 1 to n, the referenced residues range over all indices 0,...,n-1 exactly once. Hence N_k=#{0<=l<n:s_l>=s_k}. If s_0,...,s_{n-1} are distinct, their descending ranks are 1,...,n, so {N_k:0<=k<n}={1,...,n} exactly.'}, {'type': 'rotation_average', 'statement': 'Therefore, for lambda>0, (1/n) sum_{k=0}^{n-1} exp(-lambda N_k)=(1/n) sum_{m=1}^n exp(-lambda m)=exp(-lambda)(1-exp(-lambda n))/(n(1-exp(-lambda))). In particular this is at most exp(-lambda)/(n(1-exp(-lambda))).'}, {'type': 'ties', 'statement': 'Distinctness is essential for the exact uniform-rank conclusion. With ties and the weak inequality >=, if the distinct partial-sum levels have ascending multiplicities a_1,...,a_t, then every rotation based at level i has N=a_i+...+a_t, and that value occurs a_i times. Thus the average is (1/n) sum_i a_i exp(-lambda(a_i+...+a_t)), not generally the uniform-rank formula.'}, {'type': 'scale_explanation', 'statement': 'For an exchangeable bridge grouped into n equal coarse blocks, cyclic rotations have the same law. Conditional on a realization with distinct coarse boundary sums, averaging over the rotation index gives O(1/n). If each block has length L=floor(c log R) and the bridge has order R elementary positions, then n is order R/L, so this mechanism yields O(L/R)=O(log R/R), not O(1/R).'}, {'type': 'scope_limitation', 'statement': 'This is only a rank/rotation surrogate. It does not establish the actual Collatz-array marked-block bound: the useful-block event also requires a nonlow z entry, bounded positive pair totals, nonresonance, disjointness, and potentially a separate exact first-passage-conditioned law. No transfer of exchangeability or distinct boundary sums to that model has been supplied.'}]

claim_results.statement: Audit necessary occupation conditions for the open marked-block Laplace bound.
claim_results.domain: As specified in each lane; do not silently transfer a surrogate result.
assumptions: Actual reference model: Y_i are uniform nonnegative integer weak compositions of K into R coordinates. beta=log2(3)-1, K-beta R in (-15-2beta,-13-2beta). R=2J+epsilon. z_j=z0*2^(S_(2j)-2beta*j), z0 in (1,2).

Disjoint useful blocks have L=floor(c log R) pairs. C_q requires nonlow entry z>=eta, every pair total in {1,...,B0}, and nonresonance. Target E exp(-lambda N_C)<=C/R. Additional exact first-passage conditioning is a separate law issue.
claim_results.first_missing_step: Prove under the actual composition-bridge law, and separately under any required first-passage conditioning, a quantitative occupation statement connecting coarse rotations to the full useful-block event C_q with enough strength to improve the natural log(R)/R surrogate scale to C/R.
